content.text: one with a heart, i.e. a bold man). His brother James, to whom he refers in the opening of his Letter, was doubtless the one who spoke at the Jerusalem Council. This Letter is quoted or referred to by Clement of Alexandria (A.D. 194), Tertullian (A.D. 200), Origen (A.D. 230), Eusebius (A.D. 320), Jerome (A.D. 392), Ephraim Syrus (A.D. 370). It was evidently written a little before the destruction of Jerusalem.
